When a great writer and a great director meet, it's magic

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Anticipation has been building for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth for months, and the first reactions are in. Fans of Quentin Tarantino, Brad Pitt, and David Fincher, like me, can rest easy. I’ve been excited for this since I first learned the three would team up for the movie, which will be available with a Netflix subscription on December 23, but will run for two weeks in theaters starting November 25 as part of the 2026 movie schedule. Now that the first reactions are hitting social media after the movie premiered last night in Los Angeles,

I’m even more excited, especially after reading one review that subtly referred to the Tarantino-Fincher pairing as my favorite candy, Reese’s Peanut Butter Cups. Drew Taylor, who writes for The Wrap, summed it up perfectly, saying the writer and director are “like peanut butter and chocolate”:

Absolutely loved #CliffBooth — Tarantino and Fincher are like peanut butter and chocolate (the peanut butter is profane and the chocolate dipped in blood). Stop watching anything, go see it on the biggest screen around, have the time of your life. An absolute triumph. The best. https://t.co/6uUNnHPjyINovember 17, 2026

Taylor is not alone in his praise, either. Many are lauding the combination of the two, who came together on this sort-of-kinda-sequel to Tarantino’s 2019 smash hit Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood, which earned Brad Pitt his first Academy Award and is, in my opinion, Tarantino’s best movie since Pulp Fiction (hot take, I know). Courtney Howard, a writer for Variety and other outlets, calls the movie a great “hang out” film, giving flowers to Pitt and his co-stars Elizabeth Debicki and Peter Weller:

THE FURTHER MISADVENTURES OF #CLIFFBOOTH is a pure riot. David Fincher’s play at a nostalgic bygone era Quentin Tarantino loves works like gangbusters. Takes time to form, but plays like a LA film noir hangout picture. Pitt & Debicki are electric together. Peter Weller, MVP. https://t.co/njhxWdSm0fNovember 17, 2026

“Hangout” movies are among my favorite styles of movies. When they are done well, like Dazed and Confused or most of my favorite Tarantino movies (Once Upon a Time, Jackie Brown, etc.), they often become the movies I return to over and over. This seems to be another one of those. Clayton Davis, another Variety writer, also calls it one:

David Fincher’s “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is a wild, hilarious hangout movie. Brad Pitt slides back into his beloved Oscar-winning role and gives his best performance since “Once Upon a Time in...Hollywood.” Elizabeth Debicki brings an intoxicating sensuality, and Scott Caan and Peter Weller are such a treat that they could have had triple the screen time. The cinematography is gorgeous. If the 2019 film was a love letter to L.A., this one is a full-on sonnet. It’s also a nice reminder that not every director needs to write their own films, and not every writer needs to direct them. Fincher and Tarantino haven’t been this much fun in years. #CliffBooth #netflixfilm #OscarsNovember 17, 2026

Critic Josh Blumenkranz also leans into the hangout aspect of the movie, and again praises the supporting cast, including Debicki and Scott Caan:

THE FURTHER MISADVENTURES OF CLIFF BOOTH a hilarious, violent, and cool hangout movie. Brad Pitt is charming as ever as Cliff Booth. Welcome additions Elizabeth Debicki and Scott Caan also deliver. Not as good as Once but still a fun time. Love letter to Los Angeles! #cliffbooth https://t.co/lMosyYBFI0November 17, 2026

Debicki, who is probably best known for playing Princess Diana in The Crown, is getting a ton of love, with some saying she “stuns” and Jazz Tangcay from Variety calling her the MVP of the movie:

Elizabeth Debicki in #CliffBooth she doesn’t miss and is one of the film’s MVP https://t.co/yulGVidzWcNovember 17, 2026

Pretty much every reaction that I’ve read this morning is glowing, even when critics don’t think it’s as good as Once Upon a Time. Simon Thompson posted:

David Fincher’s The Further Mis-Adventures of #CliffBooth pops, throbs and crackles. Like Once Upon a Time… this is a love letter to LA. An eclectic, ragtag cast make this a slick and sexy romp. A salty and slower-burning side piece to Tarantino’s original with a fire final act. https://t.co/3izap5l2wpNovember 17, 2026

He also called it a “love letter” to Hollywood, which was the descriptor that many would hang on the first movie starring Pitt as the stuntman Cliff Booth alongside Leonardo DiCaprio. DiCaprio doesn’t appear in this one, nor do the other stars of the Tarantino classic, like Margot Robbie. This is Brad Pitt and Elizabeth Debicki, according to the reviews, and that is A-OK with me.

Could this movie land another Oscar nomination for Pitt? It’s not often that an actor gets a nomination twice for the same role, as Al Pacino did for playing Michael Corleone in the first two Godfather films. It sounds like that is definitely on the table here. I really can’t wait to check out what sounds like a really fun movie in IMAX next month.

#3748. "We've finally reached this milestone": Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP kicks off open beta after around six years preparing for cybermayhem

"Let's see how the project handles real player traffic"

After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".

As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts. In that regard, it seems more akin to GTA 4's online mode than GTA 5's, with classic improvised hijinks the main draw over being able to pull off gigs with a crew. Though, there do also look to be roleplaying servers which could scratch the itch of those more interested in pretending to be a merc than blowing up other people's rides.

"After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord. "Anyone can jump in and play now — no invites or applications needed. Fair warning: this is a true beta. Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers. We welcome everyone: regular players, future server admins, and those who just love breaking game mechanics."

"Right now, our absolute priority is stability and fixing crashes," they continued later in the post. "New features are planned, but we need to polish the foundation first. A huge thank you to everyone who has been with us since the early versions, helped with closed testing, and patiently waited. We've finally reached this milestone. Let's see how the project handles real player traffic!"

According to the modders, CyberMP's "client doesn't have a digital signature yet", which could cause antivirus software not to be a fan of it. They're also anticipating "problems with the anti‑cheat system", so it may be worth holding off on giving the mod a go if you're not keen on being trolled by someone with the sort of destructive power usually reserved for megacorps and AIs from beyond the blackwall in the Cyberpunkverse.

For info on how to get CyberMP up and running, as well as create a custom server dedicated to the likes of roleplay or races, head over to its website. As you might expect, the mod requires a legit copy of Cyberpunk bought on either Steam, GOG, or the Epic store.

#3747. Umamusume: Pretty Derby parent company plans to release seven new games by 2030 as it boasts an "88 percent hit rate" on its mobile titles

Cyberagent - the parent company of Umamusume: Pretty Derby developer Cygames - has boasted its recent successes in the mobile gaming sphere in a recent quarterly earnings presentation.

As part of this presentation (covered by Automaton), the company has established plans to launch seven "major releases" to the mobile platform by 2030. There is no word on what these games will be, but one will be released in 2027, while another two will come in 2028.

Cyberagent boasted an 88 percent "hit" rate for its mobile releases so far, with seven of its eight releases having a development budget of around a billion yen, and reaching a point where it makes that figure back every month from its playerbases. Those games include Umamusume: Pretty Derby, Final Fantasy Ever Crisis, Hololive Dreams, and Jujutsu Kaisen Phantom Parade.

CyberAgent CEO Takahiro Yamauchi - speaking during the presentation - noted that it was still difficult to predict the success of a mobile game ahead of its release. However, he also claims that the experience Cyberagent has gained with its big releases to date have allowed the company to gain a clearer perspective on profitability and sustainability.

This presentation comes after a notable month for Cygmes and Umamusume: Pretty Derby. The developer issued refunds for hotels and flights following the sudden cancellation of an LA live show for the game last month, then shortly after became a major sponsor of the Japanese Formula 1 Grand Prix. The game was also temporarily taken offline due to the major PHP vulnerability exposed last month, an outage that was thankfully short-lived.

It's possible to advance from day to night so long as you follow this one trick

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you're taking your first steps into Key Lento right now, you've no doubt realized that the day and night cycle is considerably longer than it ever was in Los Santos. So you are no doubt wondering how to change the time of day in GTA 6. It's possible, but it takes a little effort to do so.

The time of day in GTA 6 works dynamically, meaning that it gradually shifts as you're out in the world committing crimes, driving to destinations, and completing activities. There's big changes between day and night beyond the color palette change too. The police response times are a little longer at night, especially if you're far outside of a major city, while you may also find that buildings that you can enter are more likely to be occupied at night rather than day – you know, when the NPCs have jobs to be at.

So if you want to change the time of day in GTA 6 for whatever reason, the easiest way to do this is to go and rest up in the bed of your safehouse. Once Jason or Lucia is resting on the mattress, you have the option of pressing Square/X to sleep. From there you can choose to sleep until whatever time of day that you want to. A similar effect will happen if you try to fast travel in GTA 6 across longer destinations.

So that's how you can change the time of day in GTA 6, at least until you've got the story wrapped up. Once you're in the endgame, there is one of the GTA 6 cheats which is wholly dedicated to moving the time of day around – but you'll need to unlock that specific functionality before you can do so.

#3745. "Nobody was hurt" in shooting near Clockwork Revolution devs InXile Entertainment's office, the Xbox-owned studio and police confirm

"Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is currently being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.

"Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson said in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why."

"We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile said in a separate statement. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate."

InXile are set to release steampunk RPG Clockwork Revolution next year. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

Since being announced in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power."

Best wishes to the staff at InXile, here's hoping that going forwards they're able to get with making what's looking to be an intriguingly funky game without enduring any more concerning incidents like this one.

#3744. The next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console and "not a PC" says Microsoft, as it clarifies that computational power isn't sole focus this time

"It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering."

Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC". The company has also underlined the importance of using gen-AI-adjacent "neural rendering" technology going forwards, and a desire to remove "all the barriers of play that have historically existed" - notably in making the past generations of games playable.

The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday, and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald said, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.

"We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added. "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it."

Notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he said the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation.

"It's about deeper immersion," Ronald said. "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering."

While referencing the global component shortage and exorbitant prices of computer hardware, he added: "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years."

Xbox boss Asha Sharma also recently talked up the importance of generative-AI-sounding technology in Xbox's future, saying "too many ideas never become games", and that "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations".

Another key part of Xbox's Helix vision is compatibility and game preservation. "Game preservation is core to Xbox," Ronald went as far as to say. "Not only do we feel like it's the right thing for the industry, we feel a deep responsibility as one of its biggest platforms and publishers. For the first 30 years of game development, nobody really thought about game preservation when they were designing their hardware, when they were building their games." Xbox is apparently working with game-makers to ensure games can not only be played now but also 20 to 30 years into the future.

The other key facet of Microsoft's push the familiar Play Anywhere mantra, whereby one game can be played across multiple devices, maintaining your game-progress as you go. This is fundamental to Microsoft's handheld-and-console Helix plan, and something we've seen the company dry-run with the Xbox ROG Ally X handheld. "It's this notion that not only does my library move with me, but my progress moves with me as well," Ronald said. "Because I fully expect that when I'm in the middle of an 80-hour RPG, if I'm 25 hours into that and I want to play it on another device, I should be able to instantly resume from where I was. Those are things that today are becoming more common, but I think in the future it's going to be a baseline expectation of all players."

Ronald wouldn't be drawn on the issue of price regarding Project Helix - a recent report suggested Helix could be priced up to $1800 - referring to it only as both "a challenging time" but an "exciting one", because "we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable". Ronald also wouldn't reference a release date, though the report referenced above suggested the handheld Helix machine will release next holiday, 2027, and the console Helix machine the year after. The next generation, then, seems to be around the corner.

Sometimes the best thing a criminal can do is steal from other criminals.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There's a lot of ways to make money fast in GTA 6, from robbing jewelry stores, pawn shops, and banks to boosting cars, winning races, and even mugging strangers. But some jobs are more lucrative than others, and sometimes the payoff of a big heist isn't worth the time, prep work, and violence it takes to complete them. If you need some cash fast and easy, here are some ideas that are mostly low risk, high reward. Heck, a couple of them aren't even illegal!

Here's the best bit of advice you're going to get for making money in GTA 6: steal from your fellow thieves.

As you're out and about in the world, you'll often see a crime in progress: a bank robbery taking place, a jewelry store heist happening, an armored car being jacked, a drug deal down at the docks, or sometimes just a speeding vehicle filled with criminals fleeing from pursuing cops.

Hit those criminals. Hard and fast. And then take their shit. Especially in Chapter 2 and Chapter 3, another criminal's sack of bills or jewels or drugs is worth lots more than the take you'll get from hitting most robbery locations yourself. If you see crooks fleeing with duffel bags over their backs, drop 'em. (You can do it non-lethally if you like, but drop 'em.)

Then grab their bags and beat cheeks because the heat that was on them will quickly be on you. Some robbery crews will have multiple bags of goods, so best to travel as a couple, Lucia and Jason, if only to be able to carry off all that re-stolen loot and cash it in with a fence. You don't want to leave a sack of cash or jewelry behind, right? And if you act quickly enough, you'll be able to make a clean getaway.

When you're out exploring Leonida, keep your ears open at all times. Hear sirens? Alarms? Gunshots? Screams? Cars speeding or crashing? Don't hesitate. Take out the other crew and grab the loot for yourself. It's usually a great payday.

Okay, a pretty obvious one, but once you hit Chapter 2 and meet a mechanic, Moses, who gives you a slim jim and will buy stolen cars, it's probably the best way to turn a quick profit for relatively little risk. A decent car (Moses is looking for older model, low profile cars) will usually net you between one and a few thousand dollars, which is better than most smash-and-grab jobs you'll be doing at that stage and way easier to pull off. This is because Moses pays well and the fence you have in Chapter 2 does not.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The only drawback to Moses is that once he buys a stolen car, you can't sell him another for a bit. There's a big plus, though: he will often tell you precisely where the cars he's looking for are located. Randy, your car fence starting in Chapter 3, will pay way more because he's after higher end, much flashier cars.

There are lots of races with nice payouts in GTA 6, but what if, like me, you're a terrible driver? The demolition races at Ambrosia Raceway are just the thing for those of you who tend to crash a lot anyway. Win on the oval track and you'll make over three grand, and it's double the take on the figure-eight track. Plus, you can repeat the races as many times as you like. Easy money.

The secret is, you come in first by default when all the other cars have been destroyed. If you can't beat 'em, just ram 'em, flip 'em, and destroy 'em. You don't even need to use your own wheels, just rent one from the track for a few hundred, spend a couple minutes slamming your front fender into everyone you see, and pocket the winnings long before you've done the eight laps.

The hunting payouts aren't huge at first, but as you start taking on hunting missions for your old military buddy Bret in Lummox County in Chapter 2 (these missions are for Jason only), he'll request you hunt creatures that he'll pay more and more for. Like Red Dead Redemption 2, there are legendary animals in GTA 6, and that means money.

You can take down the animals from Bret's lists or just find your own prey out in the world. Just today I was exploring, spotted a large boar in the woods, grabbed my rifle from my truck, and shot it: Bret paid me $2,500 and even came to pick up the carcass himself, saving me a trip. For smaller trophies, just park outside and step into Bret's building, and he'll auto-buy the dead critters right out of your trunk. Good deal.

Your entire criminal strategy will change in Chapter 3 when you get a tool called the snap gun. This lets you pick door locks, which means bypassing alarms. From then on, make sure the places you want to rob have a back door: it's the key to turning a quick smash-and-grab into a proper heist.

Coming in the back of the store is the way to do crime: you get inside without anyone (usually) immediately noticing, can quickly and quietly subdue any security or employees hanging around in the rear of the store, get quick access to the security footage (destroy it) and the alarm system (disable it) and can locate the safe before anyone knows a heist is going down.

With alarms off and your partner doing crowd control, you can take the time to make sure you're getting every penny out of the place. Smash every jewelry display case. Threaten someone for the safe code or find it written down somewhere in the office. Empty all the cash drawers, even take people's wallets and the drugs from first-aid kits. Do it right and you can make a clean getaway, avoiding the police pursuit altogether. Beautiful.

You'll meet a pilot in Chapter 3 and he'll start offering you regular work in Chapter 4. Get in your flying practice, though: these are time-sensitive jobs.

Pete will direct you to his plane and you'll use it to distribute cocaine around Leonida by dropping packages to buyers waiting below. You'll have multiple targets to hit across the map, and a time-limit: those buyers won't hang around forever, waiting. (I guess they have something more important to do than acquiring huge bricks of coke?) Fly smart and plot your route efficiently and you'll make a nice chunk of change from each run.

There are, naturally, lots of other ways to make money, but most come with more risk, more time, or less of a haul.

One iconic movie character per actor and at a time, Pattinson!

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Robert Pattinson has had a pretty ridiculous year. Between The Drama, Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, and the upcoming Dune: Part Three on the 2026 movie schedule, he's been keeping busy. Now, as if playing the Dark Knight wasn't enough, he's officially been cast as the next James Bond. Naturally, the announcement has generated plenty of reactions, but I wasn't expecting Jon Stewart to have one of the funniest takes I've heard so far.

During Monday night's episode of The Daily Show, Stewart addressed the Bond casting while discussing a string of technological disasters and travel disruptions that had made headlines over the weekend. Somehow, he wove them all into an increasingly ridiculous story about how he was supposed to audition for 007. The lengths he went to before revealing that the Twilight franchise breakout star had beaten him to the role had me laughing out loud. Stewart joked:

I was supposed to fly out to a gig. An audition, actually. Kind of a big one. And obviously, delays at the airport. No big deal. I just thought, well, I'll just go by my preferred travel method, Mississippi riverboat.

When your flight gets canceled, logic dictates that the next step is to hop aboard a riverboat. Obviously. Unfortunately for Stewart, his backup transportation wasn't particularly reliable either, and things only got worse when he tried to contact the people running the audition. He continued the bit:

Unfortunately, we also ran into a bit of a... well, it ran into us, but... so I just thought, well, I'll let the production know I was going to be late by sending them an email from my beloved Microsoft Outlook account. And then the... uh... which... it would have been fine, as long as I could still electronically withdraw the money to rent a car, which... long story short, they ended up giving the role to [BLEEP] Robert Pattinson.

I was already laughing at the idea of Stewart missing out on a big role because his riverboat ran into trouble and Microsoft Outlook wasn't cooperating. But he saved his best complaint for last, taking issue with the fact that Pattinson already has another pretty famous character on his résumé. Raising his fist in mock frustration, the longtime late-night host shouted:

Pattinson! You already got Batman. Enough's enough!

I mean, he's got a point. How many iconic characters does one guy need? Here's an actor who has already played Edward Cullen in the Twilight movies, Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter, and Bruce Wayne in The Batman. Now he's adding 007 to the résumé. At this rate, I half expect someone to announce him as the next Superman. Hey, with James Gunn’s recent outing anything is possible.

Of course, Stewart was having fun with the news, and I don't think anybody seriously believes Pattinson should be disqualified from playing Bond because he's already Batman. But I do think it's funny that the actor is becoming the face of another enormous franchise while he's still working on The Batman: Part II.

Pattinson's casting as James Bond was officially announced Monday, following years of speculation about who would replace Daniel Craig. The upcoming 26th Bond movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, who also worked with the Die My Darling actor on Dune: Part Three. While plenty of actors were rumored to be in contention, Pattinson ultimately landed the role. The announcement has already generated strong reactions from fans, which is hardly surprising given how attached people are to the franchise.

Personally, I'm curious to see what he brings to Bond. He's spent years choosing interesting projects and taking roles that don't always seem like the obvious next step for somebody who became famous playing a sparkly vampire. His Batman was a particularly interesting take on Bruce Wayne, and I wouldn't be surprised if he approached 007 with the same willingness to make the character his own. Although now I also kind of want to hear him deliver the famous Bond introduction in his Batman voice.

Robert Pattinson's first James Bond movie doesn't have a release date yet, although production is expected to begin sometime in 2027. Meanwhile, The Batman: Part II is currently scheduled for February 2028.

Personally, I think it would be hilarious if Pattinson's next role was playing Jon Stewart in a biopic. Stranger things have happened in Hollywood, and at this point, Stewart might want to keep an eye on those casting announcements.

In the meantime, you can catch Stewart hosting The Daily Show Mondays at 11 p.m. ET on Comedy Central, with new episodes available to stream the following morning with a Paramount+ subscription.

#3740. Can GTA 6 make $2 billion in its opening weekend? One industry analyst has run the numbers, and seems to think so

We all know the story of GTA 5 making more than $1 billion in the first three days it was on sale, right? At the time, Take-Two believed this to be the fastest any entertainment property had achieved the impressive milestone - music and films included. It made history, and with ease. And it looks like GTA 6 is going to do even better.

At least, that's according to one analyst, Joost van Dreunen, a senior data analyst and great writer/numbers diviner who wrote some predictions in his respected SuperJoost PlayList newsletter. "My prediction: Take-Two announces opening-weekend sales above $2 billion by Monday, 23rd November," he wrote. And you know what? I reckon he's onto something.

Let's review what we already know: there is a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders for Rockstar's latest game floating around - something buoyed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick - and, even by the company's lofty expectations, we know the game is tracking "well above expectations" when it comes to pre-orders.

We also know a lot of people are shelling out for the slightly more pricey Ultimate Edition (£90). So many people are opting for the more expensive version, in fact, that Take-Two revised its financial forecast up to $3.5bn for the next financial quarter, thanks to "recurrent consumer spending" (something Zelnick clarified in an investor's call is explicitly linked to the Ultimate Edition). 10 million pre-orders, at roughly $100 per copy - that's $1 billion right off the bat.

"That’s two days faster than its predecessor," van Dreunen said, "and largely before anyone has even played the game." That other $1bn will come over the weekend. And then, per the analyst, the game will sell roughly another 28 million copies over the course of the first year it's on sale. "My forecast puts first-year sales at 38 million copies, only modestly ahead of GTA 5’s 35 million. The real difference may be how much revenue each player generates over the years that follow."

But it's what follows in the newsletter that intrigues me most. "At the high end, [GTA 6] may just lift the entire industry with it," wrote van Dreunen. "In the face of AI slop and shitty mobile games that exist only to extract revenue, it will offer a reprieve. At a time when the industry is increasingly focused on making games cheaper and monetising players more aggressively, Rockstar is about to demonstrate the enduring appeal of spending a fortune to make something people actually want to play."

So, even if you're dubious about the game and Rockstar's motivations for selling as many copies as possible, the launch of GTA 6 could be something that gives the industry a much-needed jolt of life, in the face of rampant layoffs and shrinking talent pools.

It's not all sunshine and rainbows ahead for Rockstar, though: amongst the frenzy of launch activity, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

#3739. GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty to 2022 Rockstar Games breach which the company claim cost them $5 million

Hacker was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital

A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.

The BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Kurtaj, now aged 21, was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial. He'll be sentenced at a later date.

Kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. The Rockstar hack was reportedly done using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into the hotel room's TV, plus a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by that hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the company contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

Earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by "Cyberleek" posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two quickly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

Hopefully with the game's console release later this week, those will be the only two GTA 6 leaks which have to be added to the annals of gaming history. As much as marketing can leave a bad taste in the mouth, especially when it barely shows anything of the actual product being advertised, neither of the GTA 6 leaks served much of a purpose beyond forcing people to waste some time and energy talking about the perpetrators.

Learn how to switch characters and issue commands to Jason and Lucia in GTA 6

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There are two playable characters in GTA 6 to switch between – Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. They are partners in crime, working together to make enough money in Leonida to build a better future. That means that you'll need to engage with both characters to get the most out of your time with the world. Thankfully, Rockstar Games has built in a number of different ways for Jason and Lucia to interact.

Whether you're playing through one of the main GTA 6 missions or just exploring the wide open world of Leonida, the game is undoubtedly at its best when Jason and Lucia are working together. Below I'm going to break down how to switch characters in GTA 6, how to meet up with your partner, and give you some top tips on how to work as a more effective pair when you're engaging in a little crime.

You aren't able to immediately switch characters in GTA 6. The option will become available once you hit a certain milestone in Chapter 2. Once both of the characters are available, hold right on the d-pad and press R1/RB to switch between the characters.

There are infrequent restrictions to swapping characters in GTA 6. Sometimes your partner will be busy, with a darkened character profile once you hold left on the d-pad indicating that you can't switch right away. Keep checking in though, as they will eventually be available.

Tip: Jason and Lucia will sometimes have their own tasks which require you to switch characters. If you see either a J or an L on the map it means that the mission must be played solo.

Checking in with your partner regularly is a great way to improve your relationship status in GTA 6. There's a couple of ways to do this, but the easiest is to message them through WhatUp – hold right on the d-pad and press Triangle / Y if there is a blue icon about a character's profile picture, or press up on the d-pad and navigate to the relevant app in the GTA 6 phone menu.

Tip: When Jason and Lucia are together, you can use L2/LT to focus on your partner. This will prompt conversations, and give you the opportunity to share items you are holding like food and drink.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Meeting up with your partner is essential throughout GTA 6. The easiest way to reach out is to hold right on the d-pad and press Triangle/Y. Alternatively, you can also navigate to the Contacts app on your phone and call your partner. This will prompt them to drive to where you're currently situated on the GTA 6 map; if you have a destination set, your partner will meet you there.

Tip: If you spend a full day together, look for visual and audio cues that it's time to head home together and get in some much needed rest. A little heart icon will appear around your residence on the map, while sometimes your partner will raise it as an idea in casual conversation.

You don't always need to do the heavy lifting on driving. If you are close to your personal vehicle, you can hold Right on the d-pad to ask your partner to drive. Once you're in the passenger seat, open up the map and set a destination, and they will start making their way there.

The AI pathfinding is solid when your partner is at the wheel, but you can hold Right on the d-pad to issue them instructions to speed up and slow down. You can also use this functionality to ask your partner to split up and take the vehicle with them –a great way of lowering your wanted level in GTA 6.

Tip: If you're at the wheel while being chased by the cops, you can switch characters to take control of the passenger. Just remember that incapacitating police vehicles (even non-lethally) will contribute to a Hardened Criminal Profile in GTA 6.

Whether you're sticking up a local convenience store for petty cash or launching an assault on a bank for a big pay day, you can undertake robberies both solo and as a pair. If you go into the map and hover over the icon of the location you're planning to hit, it'll denote the security – if it's medium to high, you'll want to consider bringing your partner along for the ride.

Before starting a robbery, hold Right on the d-pad to open up some new options for your eventual escape from the location. You can ask your partner to wait in the car while you go inside, helping to save some precious seconds before the cops show up.

Once a robbery is in-progress, you can hold Right on the d-pad to ask them to come in from the car to provide backup. Using this method is also a great way to hand over one of your weapons if they need it; each character can only hold two stash bags filled with ill-gotten gains at any one time, but you can also throw these over to your partner to carry.

Tip: Committing a robbery is a fairly intuitive process. If you directly threaten guards or cashiers, this will prompt your partner to support you and hold a weapon on them while you move through a building.

Once you're together, it is possible to have your partner leave for whatever reason. Hold Right on the d-pad to get the option to split up from your partner, leaving you solo with the character you're in primary control of. This can be done at any point while you're exploring the world, but there may be restrictions in certain missions.

If you've got the cops chasing you through the streets, you do have the option to split up. There's two benefits of this: the first is that they can split away from you and distract the cops, reducing some of the heat on you and removing one of the conditions to the GTA 6 Wanted Level you're trying to outrun. The second is that they can also head off and use one of the fences to sell any stolen goods that they have on them without you needing to be there – although, word of warning, the price you'll get for the score may be reduced.

Tip: If you ask a partner to split off from you after a robbery, keep an eye out for a message from them on WhatUp. They will usually ask if they should sell the score or come meet back up with you, and ignoring these messages will have a negative impact on your relationship.

#3737. Ever wanted to play a multiplayer version of Cyberpunk 2077 with your friends? Well, thanks to a mod now in beta, you can

You may have recently read that CD Projekt Red's in-development Cyberpunk 2 may be trying to revive the original game's online ambitions. But, if you don't want to wait the many years it'll likely be before the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel arrives, then I've got good news for you: Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta.

"After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders on the CyberMP Discord channel wrote (thanks RPS). "Anyone can jump in and play now - no invites or applications needed." The team notes, however, that this is "true beta", meaning "Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers."

Alongside the potential shakiness, the devs say it's also possible the mod could ping your anti-virus software, since it "doesn't have a digital signature yet". Whilst the priorities for the team lie in "polishing the foundations" and "fixing crashes and stability", more features are eventually planned. But for now, they stress, "let's see how the project handles real player traffic!"

So, what exactly is it? CyberMP is a dedicated multiplayer modification for Cyberpunk 2077 that allows you and your friends to explore Night City together: drive vehicles, engage in combat, and play custom community-created game modes on high-tick dedicated servers. You need an official copy of the game to play it (obviously), and the mod is completely free to download. You can download the mod, and read a fair amount of how to get it working, what to expect from it, and how to troubleshoot any issues, over at its dedicated website.

If you're thinking 'Hang on, why does Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer sound so familiar?', it's because the game was supposed to receive an official multiplayer mode after its original release. Thanks to its shaky launch, however, plans changed, and CD Projekt Red later announced that multiplayer would be a separate "triple-A release", but, eventually, that too was cancelled. The studio is still keen to honour the idea, though, and recently stated it's "focusing on bringing online into all of our franchises one day".

This isn't the first big bit of news we've had about Cyberpunk 2077 mods this week. Just yesterday, a new mod called 'Torrent' added 3D rain, lightning storms, and tyre spray to Night City - all rendered and made lovely with a new lighting system that seems to play nicely with other weather mods that have been created for the game.

#3735. Intel are being sued for "misleading" investors about "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory" thanks to AI-fuelled price hikes

Tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on.

All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they announced a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".

The lawyers in question are from Robbins LLP, who specialise in "shareholder, whistleblower, antitrust, & consumer litigation". In a press release, they say they've filed suit on behalf of anybody who bought Intel stock from July 23rd to October 29th this year.

The suit claims that Intel neglected to tell investors that falling PC and component sales were having a "materially greater negative impact" on their third financial quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Groupresults than Intel had previously stated – to the tune of "hundreds of millions of dollars" in revenue shrinkage, compared to the previous quarter, with the situation still expected to "worsen".

They also accuse the company of keeping schtum about the aforesaid "massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", together with the fact that "any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset by the negative effects on the Company’s business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup described above."

Finally, they say Intel bosses have failed to disclose that they're struggling to procure an adequate supply of substrates – that is, materials used to create the base layer of chips, circuit boards and similar components. As such, the lawyers claim, Intel couldn't "ramp up production to meet data center CPU demand even if the Company chose to divert production resources because of a slowdown in PC-related sales."

Once the Godzilla of personal computing, Intel haven't been having a brilliant few years. Back in 2024, they recorded a multi-billion dollar quarterly loss, pushing then-CEO Pat Gelsinger to resign. As regards sales of gaming PCs, they've fallen behind AMD, though they've reportedly taken some ground back recently as regards desktop CPUs. As regards graphics cards, they have long been dwarfed by Nvidia.

Any Intel investor who wants a piece of that lawsuit has until January 12th 2027 to sign up as a lead plaintiff – that is, a court appointee who represents the interests of other class members. As regards us little people who don't buy stock in huge technology corporations, all this merely continues the weird existential crisis wrought upon 'traditional' gaming and computing hardware by the feckless quest to sell a better chatbot.

Maura Higgins became a quick fan favorite on Dancing with the Stars, but I'm worried she could miss the Season 35 finals. With the semifinals and one vote before the finale, I'm afraid her run on the 2026 TV schedule may be at an end. Now, it seems I may have more reason to be concerned about what lies ahead.

On the heels of a tough Grammy night featuring the "Thong Song," it was clear Higgins' rib injury was more than a storyline for DWTS to play up. Now, per a new rumor from The Sun, Higgins allegedly had to cancel a rehearsal and seek medical attention while preparing for Dancing with the Stars' semifinals. Her rib was reportedly re-injured over the weekend, leaving some questions about how she'll be able to perform during the live episode.

As viewers learned in last week's episode, Higgins didn't break her rib, but the swelling and damage caused so much pain that she briefly considered throwing in the towel. It'd be a shame to see, given just how far she's come since the beginning, but obviously, her health takes priority.

As of late, I've written about how Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik's advancement could set up a fan favorite going home instead of them on Semifinals night. Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas were on my shortlist of people who could go home, and honestly, I think it's all going to come down to who gives the best performance.

I Thought I Knew Who I Wanted To Win DWTS Season 35. But One Comment Totally Changed My Opinion

One can never rule out the impact of fans, however, and I do wonder how this rumor could impact their thoughts on whether she should advance. Part of me thinks she could gain sympathy, assuming she wants to keep going, and get the pass to have another week to recover, give it her all, and try to win DWTS on finale night.

Conversely, I could see some viewers deciding it's her time if the performance is weak or if it's evident that she's struggling with an injury. I would see sending her home as more of an act of mercy at that point, rather than putting the pressure on her to drop out of the finale.

All this to say, I'll have all eyes on Maura Higgins as the DWTS semifinals play out. There's so much chatter happening online about who could go home, and this situation is just another layer to consider. I even think there's a possibility that Harry Shum Jr. could miss the finale, which makes the prospect of this episode so much wilder.

Dancing With The Stars airs on ABC and Disney+ on Tuesdays at 8:00 p.m. ET. This is going to be the biggest episode of the season thus far, so make sure to clear that primetime schedule to see what happens!

Everything you need to know about managing your loadout in GTA 6, including how to store and recover your favorite guns in your car

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Unlike previous Grand Theft Auto games, there are now restrictions on how you manage your loadout and how many weapons you can carry at any one time. That means you need to put a bit of effort into thinking about the sorts of weapons you want available to you, both on your person and ready in the trunk of your car.

Thankfully, it's pretty easy to understand once you wrap your head around the basics. So I'm going to walk you through everything you need to know about your GTA 6 loadout right now.

Regardless of whether you're on-foot or behind the wheel of a vehicle, you can hold L1/LB to open your loadout. This is split between Weapons and Items, and you can cycle between the two tabs with R1/RB.

On the Weapons tab of your loadout, you'll find slots for two sidearms, one for your hands, one for equipment, slots for two longarms, one for a melee weapon, and one for explosives. On the Items tab of your loadout there are single slots for: Masks, Headgear, Headwear, Outfits, Bags, Gear, Eyewear, and Smokes. You can hover over any slot on either tab with the right thumbstick and press X/A to equip.

You can manage your loadout in GTA 6 while on-foot in one of two ways:

Head over to the trunk of your Personal Vehicle in GTA 6 and press Triangle/Y to open it. From there, hold L1/LB when prompted to open up your loadout. Use the thumbstick to move to any of the slots, and then cycle through available weapons and items using left and right on the D-Pad. This will let you swap around any items that you have stored in your trunk, equip any owned sidearms and longarms that you have stored, and more. You can also stow your longarms in GTA 6 by pressing Square/X.

Open the GTA 6 Index and head to the weapons tab to locate your closest Ammu-Nation store. Every one of these locations has a weapons locker inside which you can use to manage your owned weapons and transfer them to your personal vehicle's trunk for easier access on the go.

#3732. World of Warcraft: Forever completionists push back as Blizzard gives them a powerful toy and then prepares to take it away

"Exactly the kind of FOMO that disheartens collectors."

With the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever there's a whole new world filled with niche gear and strange baubles to collect. But one item in particular has drawn the ire of the creators of a popular completionist add-on.

That add-on is All the Things, a must-install for collectors like me, as it acts as a database of all the gear, mounts, titles, crafting recipes, and super rare drops in the game. Once you collect something, it is hidden in the add-on, thus tracking your progress and making for a fantastic tool for picking the game apart.

On occasion, specific items have written notes attached by the All the Things development team, as is true of a special World of Warcraft: Forever toy, the Pouch of Violet Dust. This is a promotional item that was obtainable by watching two hours of WoW Forever streams between the 4th and 12th November.

It's a powerful toy! When used on a campfire, it changes the fire's colour to purple and extends the buffs provided by it from the usual one hour to two hours. But the sticking point with the item isn't its existence, rather the fact that it's going to be removed in early December, not long from now.

This is what the creators of the All the Things add-on don't like. "A week-long, Twitch-only window for an item that gets taken away a month later is exactly the kind of FOMO that disheartens collectors," the creators said in a note attached to the item in the mod. "It can't be earned by playing the game at all. Even those who get it don't get to keep it."

They aren't alone in feeling this way. Comments below the item's listing on the Wowhead database are equally scorching. "I love FOMO in their explicitly non-fomo game," wrote user TheWhiteRose.

"Just... Why?" added user Darrenic427. "They could very easily just patch out the camp buff duration and keep the visual effect, but Blizzard just doesn't like pretty fire I guess. Figures that they finally give us access to purple fire but then take it away after a month."

The battle between collectors and time-limited FOMO items is one that has been waged for about as long as these sorts of items have been a part of games. Though for the pouch, it's an especially weird case: an item that's cool to have but so temporary in nature that it makes it both important to completionists and strangely pointless to care about. Whether it makes a return in a later update for World of Warcraft: Forever and doesn't require out-of-game actions to obtain, and doesn't disappear, we'll have to wait and see.

WoW Forever itself is proving popular among players - me included. It's added a staggering amount of new quests and many new features to the original version of World of Warcraft, which, in turn, has injected the game with an impressive amount of new items to collect. Completionists will likely be glued to the game for a long time.

#3731. Each new GTA moves the series closer and closer to the original Mafia, the open-world game that bettered Rockstar

This week sees the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, the open-world crime 'em up that's been in development for at least eight years and has been waited on by fans for even longer. Naturally, over on PC we're still waiting for a port to be announced, let alone a release date to circle in our calendars. But, as happens whenever a new GTA is on the horizon, I think about Mafia: City of Lost Heaven.

Released less than a year after Grand Theft Auto 3, Mafia is perhaps a more prescient example of Rockstar's future than their own.

Set in Lost Heaven, a shoe-in for 1930s Chicago, Illinois, you play through Tommy Angelo's rise from a taxi driver, who has a chance run in with the Salieri crime family, to one of the gang's main enforcers in their fight against their rivals, the Morellos.

The influences on developers Illusion Softworks are obviously cinematic, with whole sequences ripped from The Godfather films and Goodfellas (and I'd argue there's a sprinkling of Once Upon A Time In America for good measure). A habit they share with Rockstar, who also pull liberally from crime films that share the settings of their games. But Illusion Softworks are also clearly interested in capturing the history of the Prohibition era, too. The story begins in the aftermath of the 1929 Wall Street Crash and the depression that followed, running through until the late 30s, and you see that time pass in the city around you. Buildings that are under construction at the start of the game are completed by its end, a used car lot in Chinatown sits empty for most of the game until business picks up with the economy, but most enjoyable of all is that the cars driving the streets change. At first the roads are filled with Ford Model-T-inspired vehicles that basically look like horse carriages with engines, but by the end of the game they've all become much sleeker creatures that have left their early carriage influences behind.

The city Illusion Softworks built also has a dedication to verisimilitude that we see Rockstar adopting in their later games. As you drive Lost Heaven's streets, you must pay attention to speed limits and red lights, as speeding and running traffic lights will both earn you a fine if a policeman spots you. For fans of public transport, there are streetcars and overhead trams you can ride to navigate the city, too. Two other touches I love: when you reload your gun, you dump the whole clip instead of returning the unfired bullets to a magic ammo reservoir, and vehicles can run out of fuel if you drive them too far.

Much had been made of all the simulations running under the surface of Grand Theft Auto 6, such as fully realised cloud formation, a smell reaction system, and… fuel tanks that can run empty. No doubt they're significantly more impressive than what's on show in Mafia, and this isn't about putting the two games against each other (even if one of them was likely made for less than the other studio spent on coffee runs across its eight-year development). Nor is it about saying history recognised the wrong game: Grand Theft Auto 3 was a huge step forward in open-world gaming and Mafia was recognised and celebrated in its time. It's about something else.

Back in 2002, Illusion Softworks offered a different kind of open-world crime game. One that was more mature despite having a lower age rating. Grand Theft Auto was undoubtedly more influential, sparking imitators that mostly opted to follow its tone and sensibilities – Saints Row began in a similar place to GTA 3 and as the series continued leaned further into the silliness and parody, for instance. But while for many years Mafia stood as a sign to an open world path that could have been taken, the longer Grand Theft Auto series has gone on, the more Rockstar have found their way toward the example set by Illusion Softworks. The games are still aiming for bombastic comedy at times, but they're also interested in the likes of newly-arrived-in-America Niko Belic, or Michael de Santa, a retired criminal haunted by his past. They're much richer protagonists than Claude, the silent character you play in GTA 3.

The Mafia series has continued, marked by ideas that remain as interesting as what was on show in the original. In Mafia 3, you play Lincoln Clay, a black soldier returned from the war in Vietnam and brought into the family. Set in a take on New Orleans, Louisiana, during the civil rights movement, you face overt racism. Linger too long in white, wealthy neighbourhoods and the residents will call on the police to move you along. And the Definitive Edition remake of the first game, released in 2020, is a rare example of a game that both captures the spirit of the original and justifies its existence by expanding and bettering the story. Though I don't think any of its sequels have been as innovative, nor as forward thinking, as the first game.

I don't want to come across as Rockstar-bashing. The studio have continued to push the open-world genre forward with every release and I want to see what other developers lift from GTA 6 for their own games. But I'm even more pleased that as the studio's aged, their work has grown closer to Illusion Softworks'.

When everything's gone sideways at 3000ft you're going to need a parachute in GTA 6. Skyscraper diving is actually what got me into playing GTA 4 online with my friends so I'm definitely buckling in for some high altitude gliding in GTA 6. Here's how to sail the skies in Leonida.

Hop out of a plane mid-air or off the top of a building and while you're in freefall press the button prompt on screen to pull your chute and float to the ground. You can steer left and right, and angle yourself downward to descend more quickly or pull back to descend more slowly.

You only need to buy a parachute one time, but you may need to reset it between uses. Head to a gun store and select it from the rack to add it back to your inventory before you go skydiving again. You can also just re-equip a parachute that you find on top of a skyscraper.

#3729. My murderous wine merchant whines for a chance at republican rule in Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion, which isn't only about the money

Longing for the Venetian Dogehouse, stuck in the Venetian doghouse

The tentacles of my trade empire snake up towards France in the west, down towards Africa in the south, and off into Hungary in the east. Yet, I still can’t reach out and grasp the throne that sits right in front of me. I’m Marco Sanudo, and the throne of the serene republic of Venice eludes me.

I’ve shed blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less. I’ve managed to avoid punishment for that crime, despite the fact it earned me a fiefdom to rule while I’ve tried to up my patrician score enough to be the lucky party the next time a ruling Doge dies in office (or runs out their 10 year term). Sadly, Doge Leonardo, the mysterious masked lord who’s had an iron grip on power since the first couple of old blokes to hold the position in this playthrough popped their clogs, is proving incredibly tough to oust.

It should, in theory, help that he’s my best mate, thanks to a well-timed feast. It certainly did in being granted a pardon for offing that other Marco, but not even that and a plague which infected nearly everyone in the realm aside from me have paved the way to Dogedom. In the meantime, I’ve striven to gain wealth and influence. I’ve worked up to having four trade routes running at once, with goods like wine, iron, and textiles flowing from market to market across southern Europe and bringing a steady supply of coin back to my Venetian estate. I’ve built trade posts at the extremities of my routes, giving me the option of starting from further afield and reaching new lands if the cash flow dries up closer to home.

This is where Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion has blended a bit with the game’s traditional feudal moneymaking to supercharge my coffers. The land holding I killed a dude for, the Proveditorate of Zara, means I’ve also had tax money from modern day Croatia to add to both my trade profits and the income my domicile generates on its own. I am, as the medieval kids say, minted.

Getting to the point of serious pocket clinkage is, as you might imagine given Silk and Silver’s focus on filling the game’s world with travelling merchant companies and wheeler-dealing republican patrician families, the beating heart of the expansion. A near-constant stream of notifications about prices of different goods I’m trying to hawk in different locations encourage me to regularly prune and re-work my routes so that max profits are being earned and no carrying capacity’s being wasted. The bubbling up of wars and plagues impacts prices in affected cities, making it a never-ending battle if you’re desperate to optimise everything within an inch of its life. I’ve found that degree of micromanagement unnecessary if the goal is just to keep a decent profit margin ticking over. Just remember to replace the trader assigned to a route if they die, recall them every few years so they don’t stress themselves to death, and check in every so often to re-evaluate whether you’re running goods that are suitably in demand.

If you stick at it for a decent amount of time, with a certain type of good - alcohol or jewellery, for example - your expertise in dealing in them increases, making it easier to sell for better prices. Trade routes left running between the same markets also gain boons from being in place for a long time, offering a counterpoint to rejigging them every five seconds to wring out a few more coins. Most of my routes have run along a path that includes stops at four markets, with the occasional location boasting a monopoly I’ve bargained for with the local ruler, so I don’t have to worry about competition at every stop.

When you’re playing as a merchant who isn’t locked into the ruling inner circle of a republic, making your routes as lengthy as possible is one of the three moneymaking areas your company can specialise in. That first one’s caravaneering, and is the one I leant into in a non-Marco Sanudo playthrough. Beyond that, you can become an expert loan shark, lending cash to rulers or paying their ransoms in order to recoup interest and collect hooks you can use for favours. Manufacturing expensive artifacts that can be sold individually to collectors for a profit is the third option. The latter two I’ve only dabbled in a little bit as of writing, having earned enough gold mostly from caravanneering to buy the land containing the city with my home market and be anointed a Sheikh. So, beginning as a landless merchant is a nice alternative to Crusader Kings 3’s long-established wandering adventurer starting point, with both allowing you to work your way up from lowly serf to landed lordly dynasty in your location of choice.

If you’re after a more specific historical scenario, Silk and Silver has Guelphs and Ghibellines. This is where we find Marco Sanudo, as well as the other patrician family head I’ve played as thus far, Speronella Dalesmanni. The setup is that the Pope and the Holy Roman Emperor have had a bit of a tiff, essentially rooted in who should have certain powers, with different cities and powerful families in northern Italy taking either the Guelph (Pope-likers) or Ghibelline (Holy Roman Empire-enjoyers) side depending on what suits their goals or principles. I’ll be honest, aside from being another way to easily earn friends or enemies in the ruthless crucible of merchant republican politics, where votes and reputation-bolstering aid from other nobles are key, the situation’s not had a hugely obvious bearing on my playthroughs thus far.

I think the closest it’s come is during my Dalesmanni run, if largely due to the existence of the By God Alone expansion allowing a new branch of Catholicism, dubbed Italian Christianity, to be created. The initial conversion push from the bishop responsible led a number of my fellow northern Italian nobles away from the Roman Rite headed by his Popeliness, making the Guelph/Ghibelline split more clearly defined.

In the early hours of both my Sanudo and Dalesmanni playthroughs, I’ve been far more focused on simply trying to push the respective patrician families up the hill from posh toffs with naught but a vote and a manor to elected rulers of their great cities, with land holdings to match. Speronella’s situation in Padua is made incredibly tough by the fact she’s a woman in a world where every succession rule is designed to put blokes first, so I’ve had more success with Marco and his quest to become the Doge of Venice.

As the head of a patrician family, one of select few elite clans who steer the oligarchical republic, I was faced with earning Marco enough respect among his fellow family heads that they’d consider voting him to the top of the succession list, thus securing his power whenever the current Doge got the boot. Pulling that off, while also not kowtowing to the requests and schemes of those same peers, isn’t easy. A large cocktail of factors go into determining whether another noble likes you enough to vote in support of your succession. There’s your patrician rating, which is upped by doing things which specifically show you to be good at this Italian noble house lark, such as establishing trade monopolies for the republic, gaining the Pope’s favour, or having close relatives who also hold key positions in the republic. However, how close a friendship you have with the target and how their character traits align with you also play a huge rule.

Thus it was that, at one point, Marco was best mates with the current Doge and had a decent patrician rating, but had only amassed 68 of the 72 points needed for said Doge to vote for him because the Doge was generous, and therefore didn’t care for Marco’s ambitiousness. That same Doge either liked or respected Marco enough to grant him a council position and the status of regent, but he would not back Marco to replace him permanently for love nor money. This is the same man who liked Marco so much that when I pulled off that not-so-sneaky murder on another noble house head in order to inherit the keys to the Proveditorate of Zara, the Doge was instantly willing to pardon me and prevent Marco suffering any punishment for the crime.

Not even a couple of serious plagues hitting Venice, which at one point had all three people ahead of Marco in the queue suffering from smallpox, could get him on that throne. Eventually, it took a bit of lucky timing when his Doge mate died of old age - a few years after beating smallpox - to finally install Marco as Doge. Given that delayed promotion, as of writing I’ve not yet had enough time in the big chair to give a proper verdict on how it differs from regular feudal rulerdom in the long run.

What I can do instead is tell you a bit about the fun of council votes. The same pool of voters who in a republic like Venice, get a say in who succeeds the ruler, also vote on the passage of laws and decrees. One proposal you can put forward is a vote to change who exactly is allowed a seat in this voting pool. It defaults to just being heads of patrician families, but can be extended to include all vassals, or tightened up so only the Doge’s councillors or the ruler themselves have a say, that being the way despotism lies. As you can imagine, passing a change to who can vote can drastically change the state of play, either tightening up the number of folks who might oppose or support you, or bringing new folks into play in a fashion that dilutes individual power, but gives you more pieces on the board to mind or manipulate to your advantage.

I’ve found it suitably tough to orchestrate successful votes to change laws and customs which medieval Italian noble families, expectedly, have firmly entrenched stances on. Getting rid of checks and balances, such as the requirement to vote on banishments or wars - so the Doge can rule as a despot - has proven one such challenge, as has changing laws governing men being prioritised over women. I tried to pass equal succession as a substitute for men being put first while playing as Speronella, but met an insurmountable wall of resistance due to the region’s culture and faith. So, all I could do was try to put my young male heir in the best position possible to make the sorts of gains I couldn’t.

Much easier to weasel into place, either through some canny swaying or the offering of hooks, are laws giving state backing or other priority to trading in certain types of goods. Alcohol, for instance, which certainly hasn’t hurt the profits of Marco’s two wine trade routes.

Thus, cash continues to flow through the tentacles of my trade empire in sizable globs. As he’s now Doge, I’ve got Marco using the ample funds of Venice’s treasury to build a new piazza and have him focused on making the city’s already-strong trade league even more formidable, by attracting new members from the few other northern Italian blocs.

While I’m fairly sure there are folks who’ll find Silk and Silver's constant barrage of trade route notifications annoying, or that their power-grabbing skills and sheer multitude of money-making means combine to make playthroughs less challenging than they could be, so far I've found it another enjoyably sonorous string to Crusader Kings 3’s bow. Above all else, playing as a merchant gives more reason to invest in stewardship skills beyond just maximising your tax yields, while the republican politics of the DLC's main region fleshes out rewarding intrigue-focused builds. Diplomacy and martial skills are less key, but still have their place at times.

If you’re an absolute stickler for historical accuracy, you may well find other things to gripe about, but aside from the Guelph and Ghibelline conflict fading into the background, I’ve found plenty to like in my quest to become top Doge.

#3728. UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch is more worried "about the amount of time" people will spend on GTA 6 than the game's violent content

"I remember in my childhood playing Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter. I didn't hit anybody after playing those games."

Leader of the UK Conservative Party (and former Mortal Kombat player) Kemi Badenoch is more worried about the amount of time people will spend playing GTA 6 rather than the game itself.

Every new Grand Theft Auto game invites some amount of controversy over its in-game violence or depictions of sex and drugs - from San Andreas' raunchy Hot Coffee mini-game to GTA 5's graphic torture scene. Ahead of GTA 6's release this week, the Tory leader downplayed those fears.

"I would be more worried about the amount of time people were spending on a game than the game specifically. I remember in my childhood playing Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter. I didn't hit anybody after playing those games," Badenoch said in a news conference shared by Sky News (good spot, IGN).

While Badenoch's stance might be surprising for the normally right-wing UK political party, she did still worry over children who might play GTA 6 for too long. There are probably far worse ways for kids to spend their time than engaging with a long-form story like GTA 6's, though, especially in an era with endless amounts of 10-second clips to mindlessly scroll past and declining funding into youth programs.

"I haven't played Grand Theft Auto, I know people are worried about the game content. At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half an hour on it and then went out and did something else. They are two different things," Badenoch added.

GTA 6's release is imminent and is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time. One analyst even suggested GTA 6 could make over $2bn in its opening weekend - that's handily more money than Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey made during its entire run in cinemas, for context.

If you'd like to reminisce a bit before the long-awaited game finally hits, you can check out our favourite Grand Theft Auto pieces Eurogamer's published over the years.

Panettiere's celebration of life happened in late September.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Back in August, the public was devastated to learn that actress Hayden Panettiere died at age 36. This was a huge shock, especially considering her brother died just a few years earlier. Fans are still mourning and re-watching her work on projects like Heroes, and plenty of people were surprised when Panettiere's mother Lesley Vogel didn't attend her celebration of life back in September. Now Vogel is speaking out and explaining her absence for the services.

Fans still have questions about Hayden Panettiere's death, and were curious about why her mother wasn't in attendance for the late actress' funeral services. Lesley Vogel recently appeared on Inside Edition, where she explained why she chose to opt out of her daughter's celebration of life. She was quoted saying:

I just didn’t want to rock the boat either; it was probably for the best.

During the interview, she shared that she and Hayden Panettiere drifted away from each other after the Scream actress' relationship with ex Brian Hickerson started picking up. They mother and daughter seemingly had a difficult relationship, some of which was mentioned in the actress' memoir This Is Me: A Reckoning. Still, it was surprising for some that Vogel didn't attend the funeral services.

While appearing in the same interview, Lesley Vogel claimed that she was indeed invited, but didn't think her presence would be helpful during this difficult time. She went on to say:

I knew that some of the people there wanted to believe I was the horrible mother because Hayden was angry and made statements.

Clearly this was a complicated situation, which might explain why Hayden Panettiere's mother ultimately decided not to attend her funeral. She knew there'd be discourse about her either way, but is seemingly at peace with her decision. Inside Edition contacted Brian Hickerson for a comment, but did not hear back from him.

Panettiere's death hit the public hard, largely because she grew up right in front of our eyes, including early roles in projects like Remember the Titans and A Bug's Life. Millennial fans in particular grew up alongside her, and there was a ton of love her work on Ice Princess, Heroes, Nashville, and the Scream movies (the latter of which are streaming with a Paramount+ subscription). Folks were thrilled when she reprised her role as Kirby Reed in Scream VI, with Panettiere thanking fans who "came to her rescue". Clearly she's someone who meant a great deal to her fans, many of whom are still processing her death. As for Lesley Vogel, she's given an explanation for missing her late daughter's funeral.

Hayden Panettiere's legacy lives on through her various acting credits. Heroes is streaming on Netflix, while Nashville is over on Pluto TV. Our thoughts continue to be with her loved ones as they mourn and grapple with the loss.
